title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 2 diabetes and concerns regarding recent hypoglycemia.

HPI
The patient is a 62-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up for type 2 diabetes mellitus. He reports that he has been managed on an oral hypoglycemic medication long-term. He expresses concern regarding a recent hypoglycemic episode that occurred while he was at home. He describes feeling shaky and lightheaded for approximately thirty minutes before consuming a snack. He denies any loss of consciousness or severe symptoms during the event. He continues to adhere to his current medication regimen but is seeking guidance on managing these occurrences.

Medication List
Metformin 1000mg daily.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented x3. He appears in no acute distress. Skin is intact and dry. Vital signs are stable.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
2. Hypoglycemia

Plan
1. Continue current dose of metformin.
2. Instructed patient on recognizing early symptoms of a hypoglycemic episode and how to treat with fast-acting carbohydrates.
3. Follow up in three months for routine monitoring.
explanations: Diabetes with hypoglycemia and no coma documented: E11.649.
Long-term oral hypoglycemic use: add Z79.84.

distractors.why: Hypoglycemia is a complication with its own code.
Z79.84 captures long-term oral hypoglycemic use.
